investigation: Identify file-backed Mimir querier RSS by process mapping

selection.limitation: Rollups do not identify the mapped file or region. File-backed RSS is not heap allocation.

ruled_out_hypothesis.hypothesis: An always-running CPU profiler causes the startup file-backed RSS.
ruled_out_hypothesis.finding: The router stores profiling configuration only. ProfilerGuardBuilder runs inside the CPU-profile request handler. The preserved diagnostic capture uses perf, not this endpoint. No startup guard is created.

harness_change: Preserve full /proc/PID/smaps for every workload role at both existing memory snapshots, alongside smaps_rollup. Run on an exact preserved release image; identify file-backed and anonymous regions offline.
next_action: Investigate the code footprint and initialization paths of the verified executable before selecting a memory optimization. Preserve functionality and qualify any change with native/caller tests and exact-image comparisons.

limitations: Rollup and mapping files are read sequentially during live load; their totals can differ.
These snapshots identify regions; they do not establish a normalized performance or memory gain.

finding: The executable code mapping is the largest resident region: 69200 KiB at start and 69772 KiB at end. It is not anonymous heap memory. Anonymous memory rises from 10400 to 30732 KiB; the large code mapping already exists after warmup.
